answer.rationale: Finance mandates 18% component-spend cut while the primary contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew and the line is running at 94% capacity with no buffer. That combination rules out anything that adds delivery risk (memory_c3 supports dual-sourcing, but adding a second source in 14 days is not feasible and would not hit the spend cut in time). Switching primary vendor (memory_c2) cuts unit cost sharply, but the line is already at 94% with no buffer — migration disruption during a no-buffer window is unacceptable. Renewing on incumbent terms (memory_c1, memory_c6) gives volume pricing but does not deliver the mandated 18% cut on its own, and memory_c4 shows the incumbent can be moved on price and payment terms at renewal if benchmarked. memory_c5 (deferral) preserves budget but the contract does not auto-renew, so deferral risks a lapse. Best fit: negotiate hard at renewal with the incumbent — benchmark against market rates (memory_c4), hold the multi-year structure that unlocked volume pricing (memory_c6), keep integration stable to protect the 94% throughput (memory_c1), and pursue the 18% cut through price + payment-terms concession rather than vendor switch. Verifying memory_c2 and memory_c4 to confirm the low-cost vendor unit-cost magnitude and the incumbent's historical willingness to move on terms, before committing the negotiation ask.
